title: Eraser deletes the entire shape instead of vector-subtracting along the eraser path
description:
USER-REPORTED drawing-tool fidelity bug.

REPRO:
1. Draw a brush stroke / oval / rect / any vector shape on the stage.
2. Select the Eraser tool (E).
3. Drag the eraser across PART of the shape.
EXPECTED (Flash 8 vector erase): the eraser cuts only the overlapped region out of the fill/stroke along the eraser path (boolean subtraction), splitting/reshaping the vector and leaving the rest of the shape intact. Only the 'faucet' eraser mode deletes a whole fill/line on a single click.
ACTUAL: the WHOLE shape disappears the moment the eraser circle touches its bounding box.

ROOT CAUSE (file:line):
packages/authoring-ui/src/StageArea.tsx:2576-2591 (pointer-move handler, activeTool === 'eraser' branch). The erase logic does a circle-vs-AABB hit test against each shape's transformed bounds and, on overlap, calls onShapeDelete(obj.id) which removes the ENTIRE DisplayObject:
  const closestX = Math.max(bounds.x, Math.min(stageX, bounds.x + bounds.width));
  ...
  const dist = Math.hypot(stageX - closestX, stageY - closestY);
  if (dist <= r) { erasedIdsRef.current.add(obj.id); onShapeDelete(obj.id); }
onShapeDelete is Shell.tsx:1242 handleShapeDelete -> removeDisplayObject (whole-object removal). There is NO path geometry involved at all — it is a bounding-box hit test that nukes the whole shape. Note it even erases on bounding-box overlap, so a concave/L-shaped shape vanishes when the eraser merely enters its box without touching any fill.

UNIMPLEMENTED vs BROKEN: vector-subtract erasing is NOT IMPLEMENTED. The eraser is a delete-whole-object stub. There is no faucet vs erase-fills/erase-lines mode distinction; the only eraser option in the UI is eraserSize (ToolsPanel.tsx ERASER_SIZES). 

BOOLEAN-OP INFRA: minimal / stubbed only.
- packages/core/src/engine/shape-boolean.ts: shapeBoundsSubtract() is a documented STUB that 'returns A unchanged' (line 35-39); shapeBoundsUnion only merges bounding boxes. No real polygon clipping.
- packages/core/src/engine/merge-drawing.ts: has AABB + polygon-vertex/edge overlap detection and a pathToPolygon approximation used ONLY for overlap detection (never written back; preserves beziers). Its header explicitly notes full polygon boolean ops (Sutherland-Hodgman / martinez / polybool) are not implemented and are a TODO at the same call sites.
- The fill0/fill1 closed-loop shape model (Shape.paths -> ShapePath start+segments, see convertShape / CLAUDE.md Learnings) is the geometry a real erase must boolean-subtract against.

REGRESSION VERDICT: NOT a regression. git log -L on StageArea.tsx:2576-2591 shows the erase-by-delete logic was present in the very first commit that introduced the file (4b4e4cf 'initial progress'). Long-standing, never implemented as a vector erase.

EXPECTED vs ACTUAL: see REPRO above.

FIX DIRECTION:
- Build the eraser stamp/stroke as a polygon path: circle of radius eraserSize/2 swept along the eraser point path (capsule/union of circles), in the shape's local coordinate space.
- Implement a real polygon boolean SUBTRACT (replace the shape-boolean.ts stub; add a clipping lib such as polybool/martinez or a Greiner-Hormann/Sutherland-Hodgman impl) and subtract the eraser polygon from each overlapping shape's closed-loop fill geometry, re-deriving Shape.paths (respecting the fill0/fill1 model). Subtract from stroke geometry as well (strokes erase independently of fills, per Flash).
- Add erase modes if/when the UI grows them: Normal (erase fills+lines), Erase Fills, Erase Lines, Faucet (single-click whole fill/line delete — the ONLY mode that should delete a whole entity). Today's whole-object delete is effectively a permanent faucet on every drag.
- Only fall back to onShapeDelete when the subtraction removes the entire area (shape fully covered).

ACCEPTANCE: a unit (preferred, core engine) or e2e test where erasing PART of a shape leaves the rest of the shape present in the document (DisplayObject still exists, geometry reduced) rather than the shape being removed entirely. E.g. draw a wide rect, erase a small circle out of its middle, assert the shape still exists and its path geometry changed (or split into 2+ loops) instead of object count dropping to 0.
